posts.text:
Why I am submitting this proposal

In June 2024, when Terraform Labs announced it was winding down, a small group of us asked the Terra community to trust that Terra could continue without a Labs company. The Phoenix Foundation was created to help secure the chain, support builders and keep the ecosystem moving forward. I still believe strongly in that mission.

As part of my role within the Foundation, I am responsible for strategic leadership and organizational oversight. That includes helping ensure that the Foundation remains capable of carrying out its mandate and that its Directors remain accountable for the responsibilities entrusted to them. Where serious questions of governance or accountability can no longer be resolved internally, I consider it part of that responsibility to escalate the matter to Terra Governance.

The issue

The Phoenix Foundation currently has four Stewardship Directors. Proposal A272, concerning the continued membership of one Director, has resulted in a 2–2 deadlock. The serious concerns behind that proposal relate to strategic alignment, governance procedures, contribution and accountability, risk management and Director-level trust.

Those concerns are disputed, and this proposal does not ask Terra Governance to decide who is right.

The immediate problem is that the Stewardship is evenly divided on a question concerning its own composition as a result of these serious concerns and cannot resolve it internally. A governing body also needs a credible mechanism to hold its members accountable when serious concerns arise. Without one, accountability effectively ends wherever an internal deadlock begins.

Proposed solution

The Phoenix Foundation Bylaws provide for the appointment of an independent Emergency Supervisor in circumstances where the Foundation’s governing bodies become unable to properly perform their responsibilities. I believe this is the appropriate mechanism here.

The Supervisor should review the circumstances and issues leading to A272, hear from all four Directors, examine the relevant internal records and independently determine how the situation should be resolved. This may include concluding that a change to the Stewardship is necessary, or that it is not. Both outcomes must remain possible.

The appointment should be strictly temporary and limited to this specific matter, with a maximum term of four weeks from acceptance of the appointment unless Terra Governance explicitly approves an extension.

I am directly involved in the current dispute and supported A272. For that reason, I am not asking Terra Governance to accept my assessment of the matter. I am asking for an independent process capable of reaching a conclusion where the Stewardship itself cannot, and I will accept the outcome of that process even if I disagree with it.

Selecting the Emergency Supervisor

The Emergency Supervisor should be chosen by the Terra community rather than by either side of the dispute. Candidates should be discussed openly before the final governance proposal is submitted.

Any candidate should meet the following conditions:

no current or past financial relationship with the Phoenix Foundation, any Director, or any team affiliated with a Director;

no pending or prior application for Foundation funding;

no current or recent role in Terra governance, the Stewardship or the Veto-Multisig;

no public position taken on A272 or the underlying dispute;

no personal or professional relationship with any of the four Directors that could reasonably be seen as compromising impartiality;

ideally, prior experience using Terra and familiarity with the ecosystem.

Two potential candidates raised:

Ray Raspberry — long-term Terra community member, on-chain researcher and investigator.

Martin — long-term Terra community member, Canadian lawyer and significant DeFi liquidity provider.

Both have been acknowledged as potential candidates by three of the four current Stewardship Directors. This should not be understood as a predetermined appointment or endorsement. The candidates are presented for community discussion, and additional candidates may be proposed.

Proposed Governance Action

By Emergency System Governance Process, Terra Governance is asked to:

Recognize the serious Stewardship dysfunction underlying Proposal A272, and the resulting inability to resolve these issues internally (2-2), as an Adverse Event under the Phoenix Foundation Bylaws.

Appoint the Emergency Supervisor selected following community discussion under Article 2.6.1.

Instruct the Emergency Supervisor under Article 2.6.3 to investigate the Adverse Event, hear from all four Directors, review the relevant records, the conduct of any Director where relevant and determine how it should be resolved.

Confirm that the Emergency Supervisor may exercise the powers available under Article 2.4.5.4, including instructing the removal of a Stewardship Multisig Member where the Supervisor determines that this is necessary or desirable to resolve the Adverse Event.

Limit the appointment to a maximum of four weeks from the Supervisor’s written acceptance, unless Terra Governance explicitly approves an extension. The written acceptance will need to include a statement of independence.

Set compensation for the Emergency Supervisor under Article 2.6.6 at an amount of up to USD 10,000, to be determined in the final governance proposal and paid from Foundation funds.

Appendices

A. Phoenix Directive

B. Phoenix Foundation Bylaws

C. Proposal A272 and Stewardship voting record:

Philipp: Yes

MB: Yes

Rose: No

Vini: Did not vote

The Stewardship has reached a question it cannot resolve internally. Rather than asking Terra Governance to take sides, I believe the fairest approach is to let the community appoint an independent person, give that person access to the full facts and allow them to reach a decision.

posts.author: 0xPhilipp
posts.text:
A272 was clear: a removal necessarily will always come with a move to 2-of-3 so one remaining Director could not unilaterally veto the Foundation, bylaws and the foundation board explicitly states that the majority decides. Routine payments passing afterwards do not erase a 2-2 deadlock on a fundamental Stewardship issue. The Bylaws are also not contradictory: the Emergency Supervisor cannot directly remove a Director, but can instruct Stewardship to facilitate removal. And the missing standing Supervisor is a separate governance issue, not a reason the Emergency Supervisor process suddenly cannot be used.

This is again a diversion into procedure instead of addressing why the proposal exists.

Community members and validators should read the actual substance and consider the risks Terra has been exposed to. While I have repeatedly been the one identifying problems, escalating them and putting out fires, serious security risks have been downplayed to the point where Terra came dangerously close to catastrophic liquidity loss.

That is what this is about: mandate, contribution, governance, security judgment, trust and accountability. Not procedural word games.

I will not accept potential legal exposure arising from potentially negligent conduct by another Director. When someone downplays existential security risks while questioning whether Terra should even remain focused on DeFi, I genuinely have to wonder whether you even hold meaningful assets on Terra yourself.

And this is exactly why Terra Governance is being asked to appoint an independent Emergency Supervisor: not to accept my version of events, but to review the internal discussions, speak with all four Directors, assess the facts independently and determine how the Adverse Event should be resolved. The proposal explicitly leaves both outcomes open.

We would prefer personal responses rather than walls of AI-generated text, but your points are pretty simple.

Three Emergency Supervisors would be okay, as long as they meet the requirements and there is broad agreement within PF (and the community). We already reached that for the two names mentioned.

However in this case a single supervisor would be a more efficient way of resolving this in a timely way so that we can get back to business. Hence the current prop asks the community to select one of 2 candidates.

An open application process can be done through this forum thread. Anyone who wants to be considered can put themselves forward, show that they meet the stated requirements, disclose any relevant relationships, and explain why they are suitable. The community can then comment openly before the final candidates are selected. I’ll also coordinate with PF so our view on whether someone meets the criteria is given here transparently. If no suitable third person can be found, the proposal will still go ahead with only 1, so it should not block the process. Target for on-chain publishing is end of next week.

PF structural changes should not be mixed into this process. The current issue needs to be resolved first.

Yes, this process can have a major impact on the ecosystem. That is exactly why it is necessary. PF needs to get back into a position where it can actually act, especially with more security incidents, infrastructure problems and fires to put out.

We need a Foundation that is pulling in the same direction and focused on protecting and growing Terra, not one consumed by internal political fights, downplaying security issues, lethargy and non-contribution or slowly turning Terra into Terra Classic through stagnation, risk aversion and an inability to act.

Phoenix Foundation is a separate legal entity governed by Bylaws drafted with MetaLeX to cover precisely these kinds of situations. Terra Governance has specific powers over funding, veto and emergency processes, but neither the chain nor an individual forum user can simply rewrite that legal framework ad hoc.

The process defined in the Bylaws needs to be followed by the Directors. This proposal is therefore an informational notice asking Terra Governance to appoint an independent Emergency Supervisor, so that the defined due process is being followed. Nothing more, nothing less.

There is a clear misconception about the role of the standing Supervisor.

Standing Supervisor = ongoing compliance/enforcement oversight.
Emergency Supervisor = temporary investigator/remedial authority for a specific Adverse Event.

The standing Supervisor is not required to investigate or adjudicate this dispute, and their approval is not a prerequisite to appointing an Emergency Supervisor. The Emergency Supervisor is the role specifically designed to independently investigate the Adverse Event and determine the appropriate remedy.

At this point, you are trying to conduct that investigation yourself, but that is exactly what the independent Emergency Supervisor is for.

The reviewer can receive the full legal documents, evidence and context. I’m not going to litigate this through endless forum questions or disclose non-public corporate material to individual users. If you want to apply as independent Emergency Supervisor, apply. Otherwise, let the independent reviewer do the job.

posts.text:
Before anything else, please disclose your identity and any potential conflicts of interest, including any relationships with current PF Directors. Given the seriousness of your accusations, transparency should apply to you as well.

As A272 makes clear, I have serious and longstanding concerns about the current Board’s ability to act in accordance with its mandate and Terra’s best interests. These concerns are supported by internal discussions.

The TLA contracts remain under ERIS administration because ERIS continues to develop, maintain and operate them. Given my unresolved concerns about the current Board, ERIS Team has not considered transferring that authority appropriate. This is not something I am trying to conceal, and the Emergency Supervisor is welcome to examine it alongside everything else.

Your accusation of coordinated voting is baseless. There is no voting agreement between MB and me. Reaching the same conclusions independently does not constitute coordination or governance capture. Similar accusations have already been made internally, and I welcome an independent Emergency Supervisor examining them alongside the underlying evidence. Serious allegations of this nature demand serious evidence, and if they are found to have been made in bad faith, that should carry consequences as well.

Invoking legal counsel and suggesting consequences for those supporting this proposal appears intended to pressure the governance process toward your preferred outcome. That is a dangerous precedent for Terra Governance, particularly when the proposal seeks nothing more than an independent review of the Foundation’s internal situation and a remedy to resolve it.

The proposal seeks independent scrutiny, not immunity from scrutiny.

Nothing in this proposal predetermines the final governance structure. If the Emergency Supervisor concludes that a five-member Board with a 3-of-5 threshold is the appropriate solution, that recommendation can be brought forward. The purpose is to establish an independent process capable of reaching conclusions based on evidence, rather than allowing those currently involved in the dispute or those looking from the outside with personal agendas to dictate the outcome.

It is increasingly concerning how much effort is being directed toward preventing that independent review from even beginning. This raises serious questions about why a process intended to establish accountability is being met with such resistance. And serious substance from A272 about chain and user funds safety is ignored.

This will be my final response on the matter, due to legal threats made. Constructive discussion appears to have run its course, and I intend to submit the proposal on-chain in the coming days so that the Foundation can move toward resolving these issues and functioning effectively again.

Validators know who has been here and fighting for Terra and who wasn’t. Don’t let Terra become Terra Classic.

Ex_TFL:

The suggestion is simple: will you make it a binding condition that any removal that does occur is only done so with an approved arrangement preventing you and MB becoming sufficient authority alone

I couldn’t care less about such a clause. I have not taken a single action that I believe other independent, Terra-aligned Directors would not have supported. (Including putting up A272)

What I will not accept, however, is a governance structure that effectively grants individual Directors veto power or permanent job security. That was essentially the outcome of Rose’s alternative proposal, previously shared publicly in a community group but since made private, which would have further entrenched both Rose and Vini and made future accountability nearly impossible.

The reason I insist on separating removal from the appointment of new Directors is simple: no reasonable candidate would want to be dragged into an ongoing governance dispute.

We have already approached two highly qualified potential Directors, including both new and former contributors, to bring fresh perspectives and experience to PF.

To address concerns about a temporary 2-of-3 multisig, I am willing to make a legally binding, off-chain commitment to vote only No or Abstain during that period, except on proposals necessary to onboard the new independent Directors. I am already KYC-verified, so I have no issue formalizing that commitment.

But the two processes must remain separate. New Directors should join to help build PF’s future, not be forced to take sides in a dispute they had nothing to do with.
